scope.idea: A causal verification must require a state transition only after an event that can cause that transition. Wall-clock waiting is not equivalent to advancing a nonce/diff-driven protocol state machine.

evidence.claim: G-004P reproduced timeout plus retry HTTP success, observed the retry winner as pending, and did not observe terminal state during a 120-second wait-only window.
After execution the host signs MsgFinishInference and adds the finish transaction to its mempool; publication is not itself application to the protocol state machine.
The user Session queues host mempool finish messages in pendingTxs explicitly for the next diff; composeDiffLocked is the state-advancing path that includes pendingTxs.
When MsgFinishInference is actually applied, applyFinishInference releases ReservedCost minus actualCost, sets StatusFinished, and records ActualCost.
The current G-004P oracle requires a successful retry winner to become terminal inside a bounded wall-clock observation window without making the next-diff trigger part of the invariant.

past.summary: G-004 observed matching request/HostStats cost surfaces but a larger escrow debit while a retry winner was still pending, motivating a liveness follow-up instead of a premature financial-defect claim.

present.summary: G-004P waits for up to 120 seconds after client-visible retry success, but the pinned protocol queues Finish for the next diff; waiting alone does not necessarily apply that Finish.

future.summary: The next proof must use protocol time: observe Finish publication, then drive or witness the next eligible state-advancing diff, and only then require terminal inference state and reserve-to-actual reconciliation.

causalPath.statement: The retry becomes client-visible HTTP success.
The executor signs MsgFinishInference and publishes it into the host mempool; this is a protocol input candidate, not yet committed inference state.
The G-004P oracle treats elapsed wall-clock time after HTTP success as sufficient cause for protocol terminalization, omitting the next-diff state-advance precondition.
The user Session retains host Finish transactions in pendingTxs for inclusion in the next diff.
During a wait-only observation window no evidence proves that a subsequent diff applied the queued Finish to the state machine.
The inference remains pending and its reservation remains visible, producing an apparent post-success liveness/accounting mismatch.
Once Finish is applied, the state machine is the layer that marks the inference finished and releases reserved surplus.

navigation.reason: The runtime symptom alone looked like protocol liveness failure; moving upward to the protocol sequencing contract shows that the verification oracle omitted a required state-advance event.

refactor.change: Replace the wait-only terminalization oracle with a protocol-clock oracle: Finish published -> next eligible diff applied -> inference terminal -> reserve/actual/balance/HostStats reconciliation. Keep any desired autonomous wall-clock finality as a separate product requirement rather than silently assuming it from the current protocol.
refactor.expectedEffect: The follow-up test will distinguish an actual stuck Finish after a state-advance opportunity from an expected pending record that simply has not yet been sequenced into a diff.
